messages:
alex_support: Hey team — SparrowHealth on Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-ded-3' reporting a sudden spike in token/sec earlier today, many calls getting 429s and p95 token latency climbed to ~1.6s. Customer saw this at ~09:12 UTC. Attaching brief repro and logs below. Can runtime/sre help triage?

lina_support_engineer: Customer provided a trace and sample request id 8f7a2b. They say the spike was very short (~30s) but enough to push them into throttling. They expect burst buffer to absorb it; looks like buffer wasn't applied.

maria_runtime: Thanks. Can you paste the admission-controller and quota-accounting lines from that window? Also pinging @jamal_sre for autoscaler logs.

alex_support: Paste from their upload:```
admission: reject tenant=sparrowhealth reason=rate_limit_exceeded tokens_requested=12000 tokens_allowed=2000 pool=eu-west-2-ded-3
quota: account_id=acct-001 delta=-10000 burst_credits=0
```: customer claims they had unused burst credits earlier in the day.

jamal_sre: Looking at autoscaler-bot: ```
[09:10:50] autoscaler: scale_decision pool=eu-west-2-ded-3 current_gpus=8 target_gpus=8 reason=stable
[09:11:40] autoscaler: scale_decision pool=eu-west-2-ded-3 current_gpus=8 target_gpus=9 reason=queue_depth_threshold
[09:12:05] autoscaler: provision_delay pool=eu-west-2-ded-3 estimated_time=26s
[09:12:35] autoscaler: scale_event pool=eu-west-2-ded-3 new_gpus=9
``` so there was an autoscale but provisioning lagged ~26s.

maria_runtime: Provisioning lag could explain the short window of throttling. But the admission log shows burst_credits=0 which is unexpected. Did billing / credit refills run? @kevin_cs can you confirm account billing/credits state?

kevin_cs: Checking billing: acct-001 monthly reserved commit OK, burst credits bucket consumed earlier at 02:03 UTC for a separate campaign. We do have a refill job that runs every 6h; next refill due ~12:00 UTC. So they had no credits at 09:12. Customer belief about unused credits might be from misunderstanding.

lina_support_engineer: Hmm, customer provided UI screenshot that showed 'available burst: 3k tokens' before spike — could be stale cache. We should reconcile UI caching TTLs.

maria_runtime: Two working lines: 1) short autoscale provisioning delay led to temporary capacity shortfall, 2) burst credits were indeed 0 at the time, so admission rejected. We should still verify that prefix/KV caching didn't amplify token usage accounting. Can you share request pattern?

alex_support: Repro steps the customer shared: 1) 150 concurrent chat completions at once, each ~80 tokens generated. 2) curl example: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-xl","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summary"}] }'
``` They use client-side fanout via 150 concurrent connections rather than streaming.

jamal_sre: Fanout of short requests can create burstiness spikes at admission. Long-lived streaming would smooth it. Also our token counting charges requested tokens at admission time for queued work; simultaneous short completions can overbook buffer.

maria_runtime: Agreed. Quick checklist: - Confirmed autoscaler lag -> Owner: @jamal_sre (investigate warm pool and prewarm thresholds). - Confirmed zero burst credits -> Owner: @kevin_cs (customer billing/credits clarifications). - Runtime: check admission accounting edge-case for concurrent short requests that may double-count in-flight tokens -> Owner: @maria_runtime.

jamal_sre: I'll also add a temporary mitigation: bump prewarm_threshold for eu-west-2-ded-3 by 1 GPU for 24h to reduce similar provisioning lag on short spikes. Will monitor.

kevin_cs: I'll message the customer with a clear timeline on credits and offer a one-off refill while they validate client changes.

lina_support_engineer: I passed recommended client changes: switch to streaming where possible or limit client-side concurrency to 40-50 while we're investigating. Customer will try a controlled replay.

autoscaler-bot: alert: increased_prewarms pool=eu-west-2-ded-3 delta_gpus=1 until=2024-06-15T10:00:00Z (initiated by jamal_sre)

maria_runtime: Quick diagnostic commands run by runtime during spike (sanitized): ```
# admission log grep
grep "sparrowhealth" /var/log/admission/2024-06-03.log | sed -n '24,46p'
# live accounting snapshot
curl -s http://internal-api/accounting?acct=acct-001 | jq '.'
```: accounting snapshot showed outstanding_pending_tokens: 14200 and burst_credits: 0 at 09:12:18.

alex_support: Customer did the replay with lower concurrency and no 429s so far. They asked if we can make admission controller more permissive for short microbursts when autoscaling is in-flight.

maria_runtime: We can consider a short 'grace window' when autoscaler signals pending scale-up for a pool: allow small extra tokens up to X% for Y seconds. Need to validate safety for noisy tenants. Adding to runtime backlog as RFC.

jamal_sre: Action items listed in thread: - autoscaler prewarm bump (in progress) - billing refill + CS outreach - runtime accounting audit (ensure in-flight token counting idempotent) - add RFC for temporary autoscale-grace-window. I'll tag progress in the follow-up ticket.

kevin_cs: I'll handle the customer communication and credit refill offer.

lina_support_engineer: Marking thread resolved for now; will re-open if customer sees another spike after client changes and our mitigations. :white_check_mark:
